title: Phantom Blade Zero Side Quests - What Can Open Paths, And What Can Be Missed
description: Side quests in Phantom Blade Zero: S-GAME says completing some opens paths through the story, community coverage warns some cannot be recovered, and one evidenced branch changes a boss fight. No quest names exist yet.
keyword: phantom blade zero side quests, pbz sidequest, phantom blade zero missable side quests, phantom blade zero quest list, phantom blade zero exploration

facts.label: Do side quests matter?
facts.value: Yes - S-GAME states that interacting with people and completing some side quests may open paths through the story

facts.label: Can any be missed?
facts.value: Community coverage says some cannot be recovered once missed; none is named yet

facts.label: Quest hub
facts.value: Pang Town (庞镇) - the settlement where martial artists from across the Wulin have gathered

facts.label: Tracking
facts.value: The game shows per-map collectible totals, a list of what you have taken, and a completion percentage

facts.label: Gating
facts.value: Some areas need a specific Phantom Edge, and gated spots are marked on the map

facts.label: One evidenced branch
facts.value: In the July 2025 test build, choosing to skip a red-dressed adversary changed the Seven Stars fight from a duel into a paired encounter

sections.title: The Short Answer
sections.content:
Side content is load-bearing in this game, and no list of it exists yet. S-GAME's own State of Play essay says that interacting with people and completing some side quests may open paths through the story - which in a game with a reported eight endings means a skipped quest can plausibly mean an unseen branch. The community wiki goes further and states plainly that some side quests cannot be recovered once missed.

What nobody has before release: quest names, a quest log layout, counts per region, or which specific quests gate which content. Any site publishing a numbered side-quest list on 27 October is writing fiction, including the ones that look confident and tabulated.

sections.title: How Quests Sit Inside The Map Structure
sections.content:
The world is built as large handcrafted maps joined seamlessly, filled out with side content - the studio calls it wide-linear rather than open world, and community coverage describes it as a wide-linear flow with light Metroidvania-style exploration. That shape has three consequences for questing:

  • Exploration is the quest delivery. Regions are populated by bells, challenge locations, collectibles and NPCs rather than by markers on an open map; see locations and collectibles.
  • Some areas are locked behind tools. Reaching certain spots needs a specific Phantom Edge, so a region you can partially walk is not necessarily finished.
  • The game tells you what you missed on a map. Per-map totals, a pickup list and a completion percentage exist, and spots needing a specific Phantom Edge are marked. That percentage is the closest thing to a missable detector available before a quest log is documented.

sections.title: Pang Town Is The Hub To Clear First
sections.content: Pang Town (庞镇) is the settlement where martial artists from across the Wulin have gathered, described in the deep dive as a trap of rival factions and hidden malice rather than a rest stop. Community coverage ties side quests to its NPCs specifically, which makes it the one place where a "clear it before advancing" rule is worth following even without a named list: hub populations are the usual first casualty of chapter transitions in this genre.

sections.title: One Branch Is Actually Documented
sections.content:
The July 2025 showcase build is the only place a choice with a mechanical consequence has been described, and it is worth reproducing carefully because it shows what the official claim about side content looks like in practice.

In coverage of that test build, an encounter with a red-dressed adversary could be fought on the spot or left alone. Fighting it led to a straight one-on-one at the Seven Stars formation; skipping it produced a paired boss encounter instead - coverage describes the second version as considerably harder.

Three caveats, all of them load-bearing. It was a demo build with roughly half the area, no skill tree and no weapon upgrades, and with weapon acquisition reordered. The source is a preview write-up, not S-GAME's documentation. And the shipped game may have changed the trigger entirely. So read it as evidence that choice-driven boss difficulty exists in the design, not as a walkthrough step.

sections.title: How Not To Miss Things Without A Quest List
sections.content:
1. Follow the map percentage, not the markers. A map that stops climbing is the signal; the completion screen lists what remains.
  2. Take every Phantom Edge you find, even ones you would never equip. They are keys as much as weapons.
  3. Clear Pang Town NPCs before advancing a chapter, and talk to anyone who moves.
  4. Touch every bell. They reveal fog, restock combat resources and serve as fast travel - see collectibles.
  5. Pick a difficulty you can actually finish. The director moved the death countdown into 66 Days precisely because applying it to a first run was too harsh; that is an explicit invitation to see the story first and the challenge second.
  6. Plan a second run. New Game Plus carries weapons and upgrades, and the late-game arsenal was built to be used there.

The wider risk list, including what permanent failure looks like in 66 Days and how saving works, is on missable content.

sections.title: What This Page Fills In At Launch
sections.content:
• Quest names and per-region counts, which no source has published.
  • Which quests gate which ending. The eight-ending figure is repeated coverage, not confirmation - see endings.
  • The real missable list, replacing the current "some exist, none named" statement.
  • Whether the red-dress branch survives into the shipping game, and whether it is the only one of its kind.

Reviewers finished the game a week early and mostly criticised the story's legibility rather than its structure, so a quest map should exist within days of release. This page is the placeholder that turns into it.

sections.title: Sources
sections.content: Compiled 27 October 2026 from: S-GAME's State of Play deep dive (11 August 2026) for the claim that side quests open story paths; the 影之刃 WIKI on BWIKI (fan wiki, unaffiliated with S-GAME, last edited 13 October 2026) for the warning that some side quests cannot be recovered and for the map-structure and bell behaviour; and press coverage of the July 2025 Beijing showcase for the red-dress branch, quoted above with its demo-build caveats attached. Each boss and region claim on this page is cross-linked to the page carrying its own source.
